name: AlmaLinux
notes: RHEL-compatible rebuild. Mostly used for servers; a desktop is optional.

name: Alpine Linux
notes: Uses musl libc and BusyBox, so some proprietary software will not run.
In setup-alpine choose disk mode 'sys' for a normal disk install ('diskless' runs from RAM, 'data' only prepares a data disk).
install_steps: Boot the Alpine ISO and log in as 'root' (no password).
Run: setup-alpine and answer the prompts (keyboard, hostname, network, root password, time zone, mirror, SSH).
When asked for the disk, pick your target disk and the 'sys' mode. The script partitions it automatically; the layout above shows what a manual setup should look like.
Reboot, remove the USB stick and log in with the account you created.

name: Arch Linux
notes: The live ISO includes 'archinstall', a guided text installer that follows the same layout.
Secure Boot is possible only with manual key setup; disable it for a first install.
install_steps: Boot the Arch ISO, set the keyboard (loadkeys), and confirm boot mode: ls /sys/firmware/efi/efivars (a listing means UEFI).
Connect to the network (iwctl for Wi-Fi) and sync the clock: timedatectl set-ntp true
Partition, format and mount the disk with the commands below.
Install the base system: pacstrap -K /mnt base linux linux-firmware (add your CPU microcode, a text editor and networkmanager).
Generate fstab: genfstab -U /mnt >> /mnt/etc/fstab, then arch-chroot /mnt.
Inside the chroot: set time zone, locale, hostname, root password, install a boot loader (GRUB or systemd-boot), enable NetworkManager.
Exit, unmount with umount -R /mnt and reboot.

name: Asahi Linux
notes: Only for Apple Silicon Macs. It cannot be installed on Intel PCs or other ARM boards.
The installer runs from macOS and resizes the macOS container; no manual partitioning is needed.
steps: Update macOS and make a full backup first.
Follow the install instructions on the Asahi Linux website (the installer is started from macOS Terminal).
Choose how much space to give Linux, pick the desktop flavour, and follow the prompts, including the 1TR recovery steps.
Reboot, hold the power button to open the boot picker and choose the new Linux entry.

name: BlackArch Linux
installer: BlackArch installer (live ISO) or add the repo to Arch
notes: A penetration-testing distribution. The full tool set takes tens of GB, so plan a large root partition.
Alternative: install plain Arch, then add the BlackArch repository and the tool groups you need.
install_steps: Boot the BlackArch live ISO.
Start the installer from the live environment (see the instructions on blackarch.org).
Partition with the layout above, choose the tool set and a user account, then install.
Reboot and remove the USB stick.

name: CentOS Stream
notes: Rolling preview of the next RHEL minor release; it is not a stable RHEL clone.

name: Clear Linux
notes: Intel has announced that the project is no longer supported. Existing images still boot but receive no updates, so it is not recommended for new installs.
install_steps: Boot the live image and run the installer.
Choose manual partitioning if you want the layout above, then follow the prompts.

name: CloudLinux OS
installer: Anaconda (or convert an existing CentOS/Alma system)
notes: Commercial server OS for shared hosting; a license is required.
Most people convert an existing RHEL-compatible server using the vendor's conversion script instead of a fresh install.

name: Debian
notes: Use the non-free-firmware image if your Wi-Fi or GPU needs firmware.
The installer's 'Guided' mode is fine for most people; use 'Manual' to follow the layout above.

name: EndeavourOS
notes: Arch-based with a friendly installer. The installer can download a desktop of your choice (online mode).

name: elementary OS
notes: Ubuntu LTS based. An SSD is recommended.

name: Fedora
notes: Workstation uses Btrfs with subvolumes (root and home share one pool) and swap on compressed RAM (zram).
Hibernation needs a real swap partition; tick 'hibernate' if you want that.

name: Garuda Linux
notes: Defaults to Btrfs with automatic snapshots and zstd compression.

name: Gentoo
notes: Source-based: large installs compile for hours. Binary packages and a binary kernel (gentoo-kernel-bin) reduce that.
Only the partitioning step is automated here. Follow the Handbook for the rest.
install_steps: Boot any recent live image (the Gentoo minimal ISO is best) and check boot mode.
Partition, format and mount the disk with the commands below (mount root on /mnt/gentoo).
Download and unpack a stage3 tarball into /mnt/gentoo as the Handbook describes.
Copy DNS info, mount /proc, /sys and /dev, then chroot into /mnt/gentoo.
Configure make.conf, choose a profile, sync with emerge-webrsync, then update @world.
Install a kernel (gentoo-kernel-bin is the quickest), firmware and fstab entries.
Install and configure a boot loader, set the root password, then reboot.

name: Kali Linux
notes: Designed for security testing, not as a general daily system.
Secure Boot is not supported by the standard images; disable it in firmware.

name: Knoppix
notes: Mainly used as a live rescue system. Installing it to a disk is possible but unusual.
steps: Write the Knoppix image to a USB stick or DVD.
Boot it; the whole system runs from the stick with no changes to the internal disk.
Optional: use the installer from the menu to copy it to a disk, or save settings to a persistent image on the USB stick.

name: Linux Mint
notes: Good first distro. Ubuntu LTS based. Swap is a file by default in the installer's guided mode.

name: Lubuntu
notes: Lightweight Ubuntu flavour using LXQt. A good fit for older machines.

name: Mageia
notes: RPM-based community distribution (Mandriva heritage) with its own installer and Mageia Control Center.
install_steps: Boot the USB stick (the Live ISO includes the installer icon; the classic DVD boots straight into DrakX).
Accept the license, pick language, then choose 'Custom' disk partitioning to apply the layout above (or 'Use free space' for dual boot).
Choose desktop and packages, set the root password and create a user.
Install the boot loader (GRUB2-EFI on UEFI), reboot and remove the USB stick.

name: Manjaro
notes: Arch-based but with delayed, tested updates. Secure Boot is not supported; disable it.

name: MX Linux
notes: Debian stable based and light on resources. Uses its own installer with good manual partition support.

name: Navy Linux
notes: No reliable information was collected for this distribution. A generic layout is shown, but you should confirm requirements and the installer from the project's own documentation before using it.

name: NixOS
notes: The Nix store grows quickly, so give root generous space and plan to run garbage collection.
Secure Boot needs extra tooling (for example lanzaboote); disable it for a first install.
install_steps: Boot the graphical ISO (easiest) or the minimal ISO (manual, uses the commands below and nixos-generate-config).
In the graphical installer choose language, location, keyboard and desktop, then pick 'Manual partitioning' to apply the layout above.
Create a user and choose whether to allow unfree software (needed for NVIDIA drivers).
Install and reboot. Your system is described in /etc/nixos/configuration.nix.

name: openSUSE
notes: Leap is the stable release, Tumbleweed is rolling. Both default to a Btrfs root with snapshots.
If the root partition is under about 40 GB, disable snapshots or use XFS/ext4 to avoid running out of space.

name: Oracle Linux
notes: RHEL-compatible; free to download and use. Offers the Red Hat compatible kernel or Oracle's UEK kernel.

name: Pop!_OS
notes: A clean install normally creates a 4 GiB recovery partition in addition to the layout shown. Add it if you want the Refresh Install feature.
The NVIDIA ISO includes the proprietary driver; pick it on NVIDIA systems.

name: Raspberry Pi OS
installer: Raspberry Pi Imager (writes a disk image)
notes: No manual partitioning. The image creates a FAT boot partition (about 512 MiB) and an ext4 root that expands to fill the card on first boot.
For a regular PC use Debian or another distribution instead.
steps: Install Raspberry Pi Imager on another computer.
Choose your Pi model, the OS (Raspberry Pi OS 64-bit for Pi 3 and newer), and the storage (microSD, USB or NVMe).
Open the OS customisation options and set hostname, user, Wi-Fi and SSH.
Write the image, insert the card/drive into the Pi and power it on.

name: Red Hat Enterprise Linux
notes: Needs a Red Hat account. A no-cost developer subscription is available for individuals.

name: Rocky Linux
notes: RHEL-compatible rebuild. Mostly used for servers.

name: Scientific Linux
notes: The project has ended and receives no updates. Use AlmaLinux or Rocky Linux for new installs.

name: Slackware
notes: A full install (all package sets) is recommended and takes around 15 GB or more.
install_steps: Boot the Slackware DVD or USB and log in as 'root'.
Partition with cfdisk/fdisk (or use the commands below).
Run: setup
In setup choose ADDSWAP, TARGET (set the root and ESP mount points), SOURCE, SELECT (full install recommended) and INSTALL.
In CONFIGURE choose the kernel, boot loader (ELILO/GRUB on UEFI, LILO on BIOS), network and root password.
Exit setup and reboot.

name: SUSE Linux Enterprise
notes: Commercial; a registration code (or a trial) is needed for updates. SLES defaults to a Btrfs root with snapshots.

name: Tails
notes: Tails runs from a USB stick and leaves the computer's disk untouched. It is not installed to the internal drive.
A USB stick of at least 8 GB is required; encrypted Persistent Storage is optional.
steps: Follow the official installation steps on the Tails website to write the image to a USB stick and verify the download.
Boot the target computer from that USB stick.
Optional: create an encrypted Persistent Storage on the remaining USB space from the Welcome screen.

name: Tizen
notes: Tizen targets TVs, wearables and embedded devices, and it is flashed by the device maker. There is no standard PC install, so no partition plan is shown.
steps: For app development, install Tizen Studio and use its emulator.
For hardware images (for example the Raspberry Pi builds), follow the project's flashing guide for that specific board.

name: Ubuntu
notes: Ubuntu creates a swap file by default instead of a swap partition.
Server edition needs much less (about 1 GB RAM and 5 GB disk).

name: Void Linux
notes: Uses runit instead of systemd. The base ISO is text only; the XFCE image adds a desktop.
install_steps: Boot the Void live ISO and log in as 'root' (the password is 'voidlinux').
Run: void-installer
Work through the menu: Keyboard, Network, Source (local), Hostname, Locale, Timezone, RootPassword, UserAccount, BootLoader.
In Partition, use cfdisk to create the layout above; in Filesystems assign mount points and formats.
Choose Install, then reboot.

name: VzLinux
notes: RHEL-compatible server OS from Virtuozzo. Many people convert an existing CentOS/Alma system instead of installing fresh.

name: Zorin OS
notes: Ubuntu LTS based and aimed at Windows switchers. Core, Lite and Pro editions have slightly different needs.

name: Peppermint OS
notes: Lightweight, Debian based, with a focus on web apps.
